+### Execution Modes
+
+Both `eval_string/3` and `eval_file/3` support two execution modes:
+
+* **`:safe` (default)** — Restricts templates to structured Stem expressions, literals, helpers, and variable paths. Forbids arbitrary Elixir code. This is the recommended mode for all production templates and protects against Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI). Use this for:
+  * User-generated or untrusted template sources
+  * Production environments
+  * Compliance-sensitive applications
+
+* **`:permissive`** — Allows arbitrary Elixir expressions. Provides maximum flexibility but should only be used for development and local experiments when the template source is entirely trusted and controlled by your own team. Passing `mode: :permissive` serves as a visible code-review flag during security review.
+
+```elixir
+# Safe by default — use in production
+Stem.Unsafe.eval_string("{{user.name |> trim |> upcase}}", assigns: [user: %{name: "nina"}])
+
+# Explicit opt-in for arbitrary code — development only
+Stem.Unsafe.eval_string("{{a + b}}", assigns: [a: 1, b: 2], mode: :permissive)
+```
+
+Additional features:
+- `contract:` lets templates declare required assigns at the call boundary
+- Helper pipelines are safe-mode compatible because they lower to helper invocations instead of arbitrary Elixir

 == Security and HTML Escaping
 
-Stem does not perform automatic HTML escaping; `{{ expression }}` renders the expression result directly as a string.
-Any output transformation, including sanitization and escaping, must be done explicitly through helper functions (e.g., `{{name |> escape_html}}`) or ordinary Elixir function calls used in expressions.
+Stem is **secure by default**: `{{ expression }}` output is **automatically HTML escaped** to prevent XSS attacks.
+Use `{{{ expression }}}` for raw output only when you know the content is safe.
 
-Keeping the rendering model to one expression form removes ambiguous output modes and makes security-sensitive formatting decisions explicit at the call site.
-Callers must treat all dynamically selected templates and user-provided context as untrusted, applying sanitization at the output boundary.
+Escape modes can be configured globally via `.stem.config.json` or per-call:
+
+* **HTML escaping (default)** — Prevents XSS attacks
+* **Raw output (`:none`)** — Use with caution only for trusted content
+* **Other modes** — `:xml`, `:json`, `:url`, or custom escape functions
+
+Keeping the rendering model explicit makes security-sensitive formatting decisions visible at the call site.
+Callers must treat all dynamically selected templates and user-provided context as untrusted.
+
+== Execution Modes: Safe vs. Permissive
+
+Stem enforces two execution modes for template evaluation:
+
+* **`:safe` (default, recommended)** — Restricts templates to structured Stem expressions, literals, helpers, and variable paths. Forbids arbitrary Elixir code. Protects against Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI). This is the required mode for all production templates.
+
+* **`:permissive`** — Allows arbitrary Elixir expressions. Maximum flexibility but should only be used for development and local experiments when the template source is entirely trusted and controlled by your team. Passing `mode: :permissive` serves as a visible code-review flag.
+
+Runtime evaluation APIs (`Stem.Unsafe.eval_string/3` and `Stem.Unsafe.eval_file/3`) default to `:safe` mode, requiring explicit opt-in to use `:permissive`.
+If you feel forced to use `:permissive` in production, this indicates an architectural flaw: business logic is leaking into the presentation layer and should be refactored into helpers or backend services.

+=== ADR-0004: Two-Mode Execution Model for SSTI Protection
+
+Accepted (2026-05-22).
+
+*Context.* Runtime template evaluation introduces Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) risk. Stem must make the trust boundary explicit and force developers to consciously opt into unsafe behavior.
+
+*Decision.* Implement two execution modes: `:safe` (default) forbids arbitrary Elixir expressions and restricts templates to structured Stem expressions, literals, helpers, and paths; `:permissive` allows arbitrary Elixir code for trusted internal templates. Runtime evaluation APIs (`eval_string/3`, `eval_file/3`) default to `:safe` and require explicit `mode: :permissive` in config or at the call site to enable unrestricted code.
+
+*Consequences.* Production templates are protected against SSTI by default. The requirement to explicitly set `mode: :permissive` serves as a visible code-review flag. +=== Execution Modes
+
+The CLI supports two execution modes via the `--permissive` flag:
+
+*Safe Mode (default):*
+[source,sh]
+----
+# Restricts templates to structured Stem expressions only
+echo '{"name":"Nina"}' | bin/stem template.stem
+----
+
+*Permissive Mode:*
+[source,sh]
+----
+# Allows arbitrary Elixir expressions — development only
+echo '{"a":1,"b":2}' | bin/stem template.stem --permissive
+----
+
+Use `:safe` mode (the default) for all production templates and when working with untrusted or user-generated templates.
+Only use `--permissive` for local development and experiments on templates you fully control.
+
+== Runtime APIs
+
+Stem provides runtime evaluation APIs for dynamic template compilation:
+
+[source,elixir]
+----
+# Safe by default — structured Stem expressions only
+Stem.Unsafe.eval_string("Hello {{name}}", assigns: [name: "Nina"])
+
+# Explicit opt-in for arbitrary Elixir — development/trusted sources only
+Stem.Unsafe.eval_string("{{a + b}}", assigns: [a: 1, b: 2], mode: :permissive)
+----
+
+Always use `:safe` mode (the default) for production templates.
+Only pass `mode: :permissive` when the template source is entirely controlled by your team and arbitrary code execution is necessary.
+
+For full API reference, see xref:architecture:index.adoc[Architecture] documentation.
+
+== Security Best Practices
+
+* **Always use `:safe` mode in production.** It is the default for a reason.
+* **Never execute user-generated templates.** If you must, ensure they are validated and safe first.
+* **Use HTML escaping by default.** `{{ expression }}` is escaped; use `{{{ expression }}}` only for trusted content.
+* **Inject all data via `assigns`.** Do not allow templates to read environment variables or access global state.
+* **Register custom helpers instead of relying on `:permissive` mode.** Helper functions keep business logic out of templates.
+
 == Relationship To The Other Docs
 
 * Keep project orientation in xref:onboarding:index.adoc[Onboarding].

@@ -11,10 +11,18 @@ Stem templates act as purely declarative views. They have zero direct access to
 #### Why
 Allowing templates to access global state or execute arbitrary logic violates separation of concerns, tangling generation logic with presentation code. Enforcing a strict boundary keeps templates portable, reusable, and secure against data-exfiltration Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) attacks. Templates act as exemplars of the desired output with holes where the programmer sticks values — nothing more.
 
+The [[safe-mode]] execution mode enforces this boundary at compile time by forbidding arbitrary Elixir expressions, ensuring templates remain purely declarative.
+
 #### How
 Fetch all necessary data (API URLs, database records, configuration flags) in the Elixir controller and pass it explicitly via the `assigns` keyword list to your compiled template macros or `Stem.Unsafe` runtime functions. Do not call Elixir system or I/O functions from inside `.stem` files. The compiler's default `mode: :safe` enforces this boundary at compile time.
